page: Hetzner Cloud ccx23 is a dedicated-vCPU virtual server belonging to the provider's general-purpose family. Powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, the instance delivers 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores utilizing simultaneous multithreading. It features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware instruction support includes AVX, AES, SHA_NI, and BMI2, though AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. System memory is sized at 16.0 GB, providing an even 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 3.91 GB per thread. The server is bundled with 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and operates without an attached accelerator or complimentary public IPv4 address under a QEMU hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-threaded performance combined with stable multi-core scaling. The instance reaches top-quartile results in stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core assessments, alongside high throughput in bzip3 decompression and text processing. Multi-core performance aligns with its 4-thread envelope, posting average results in PassMark CPU score, software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and image processing. Conversely, aggregate multi-threaded output is bounded by the core count, reflecting lower relative results in multi-core stress-ng, PassMark database operations, and Redis SET throughput at 4.05 million operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 36.09 GB/s for uncached reads and 27.85 GB/s for writes, supporting small-scale machine learning generation tasks up to 153.33 tokens per second on lightweight models.

Because compute threads are dedicated rather than shared, the ccx23 eliminates noisy-neighbor variance and avoids CPU credit throttling. The bundled combination of dedicated cores, balanced memory density, and local NVMe storage provides steady efficiency for compute tasks that cannot tolerate latency spikes. Tradeoffs include modest memory bandwidth on uncached datasets, the lack of AVX-512 acceleration, and throughput limitations in heavy transactional database workloads. The instance is suited for CI/CD build environments, code compilation, general web and API serving, application backends, and batch ETL jobs.
description: Hetzner Cloud ccx23 is a general-purpose virtual server configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz across two physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory allocation of approximately 3.91 GB per thread, alongside 160 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. It operates without an attached GPU under a QEMU hypervisor on x86_64 architecture. Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread execution, evidenced by top-quartile performance in stress-ng and Geekbench single-core evaluations. However, total throughput is limited by its four-vCPU count, resulting in modest multi-core scores, lower database operations, and constrained Redis throughput. The server provides predictable, unshared CPU capacity without hardware overcommit, making it a reliable choice for sustained application execution, development environments, CI/CD runners, and mid-tier backend services requiring dedicated core access.
